subject.title: fix(cron): expose flat cron job fields and normalize malformed tool args

question: Should OpenClaw advertise `model`, `fallbacks`, `toolsAllow`, and `timeoutSeconds` as flat model-facing cron add/update fields while rejecting shell/on-exit fields and leaving `contextTokens`/`maxSpendUsd` to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/64721?
rationale: The implementation matches existing cron runtime fields, but exposing provider selection and tool allow-list controls to model-generated scheduled turns is a product and security-boundary decision rather than a mechanical repair decision.

options.title: Accept the narrow flat repair
options.body: Land this PR as the supported flat schema for `model`, `fallbacks`, `toolsAllow`, and `timeoutSeconds`, and keep context/spend controls separate.

options.title: Narrow the flat surface
options.body: Require the PR to advertise only schedule and message fields, leaving provider routing and tool access overrides for a later maintainer-authored contract.

options.title: Pause for the wider cron contract
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers decide the full scheduled agent-turn payload contract, including context and spend controls.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow flat repair
recommendation.body: Land this PR as the supported flat schema for `model`, `fallbacks`, `toolsAllow`, and `timeoutSeconds`, and keep context/spend controls separate.

likelyOwner.reason: mmaps has the clearest merged history on scheduled-turn tool policy, and the most sensitive open choice is flat `toolsAllow` exposure.
